title: Breakfast Burrito Bar
shortDescription: Build burritos before the rig rolls
subtitle: Build burritos before the rig rolls
description: Build burritos before the rig rolls. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Crisp the hash browns
steps.instruction: Heat a large griddle or two skillets over medium-high. Spread hash browns in an even layer, pressing down with a spatula; let brown 8–10 minutes before flipping in sections.

steps.title: Brown the sausage and vegetables
steps.instruction: In a separate pan, brown sausage or chorizo, breaking it into crumbles. Add onion and peppers; cook until softened and the sausage is fully cooked through. Drain excess fat.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt. Scramble gently over medium heat until just set; fold in half the cheese off heat so it melts without turning rubbery.

steps.title: Set up the burrito bar
steps.instruction: Warm tortillas wrapped in foil in a low oven. Lay out hash browns, sausage mix, eggs, remaining cheese, salsa, and hot sauce in separate pans so the crew builds their own.

steps.title: Roll and hold
steps.instruction: Fill and roll burritos, tucking in the sides first, then rolling forward tight. Hold finished burritos seam-side down on a sheet pan in a 200°F oven so the line stays hot as people filter through.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Label every topping bowl — rookies grab faster when they can read the line.
Keep hot bases (potatoes, chips) in lidded containers at 200°F and cold toppings on ice if service runs long.
Put forks, napkins, and a trash can at the end of the bar — self-serve feeds get messy fast.
Keep hot items on one side of the table and cold on the other — eggs stay hot, fruit stays cold.
Line up Breakfast Burrito Bar on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Build burritos before the rig rolls. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
